knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Backend-specific index validation gap in index-based selection and embedding lookup operations
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Different backends may not enforce the same input validation rules as reference backends, causing invalid indices to succeed silently and return incorrect results instead of raising errors.

risk_dimensions.shape: Index values at or beyond valid dimension boundaries; varying selected dimension sizes; degenerate or zero-size selected dimensions.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer index tensor dtype variations may expose backend-specific validation or indexing behavior.
risk_dimensions.memory: No explicit memory layout trigger identified; index tensor storage layout may vary across backends.
risk_dimensions.device: MPS backend may diverge from CPU reference validation behavior for index-based operations.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Operation may succeed without exception for invalid indices depending on backend execution state.

failure_mechanism.description: Backend-specific implementations may omit index bounds validation before performing lookup or selection, allowing invalid indices to produce invalid results without raising an exception.

input_exploration: Explore index values at and beyond valid boundaries, including maximum valid, maximum valid plus one, and negative out-of-range values.
Vary selected dimension sizes and embedding table row counts to change the valid index range.
Vary index tensor lengths and integer dtypes to expose backend validation differences.
constraint_awareness: Run equivalent operations on a strict reference backend such as CPU to establish expected exception behavior.
Ensure index values are validated against the selected dimension size or embedding table range.
Account for backend-specific execution paths that may skip validation.
oracle_strategy: Compare exception behavior between target backend and reference backend; flag cases where the reference raises an error but the target returns a tensor.
Compare output values against reference outputs for boundary and out-of-range indices.
Monitor for silent invalid results when no exception is raised by the target backend.

transferability.reason: The principle applies broadly to index-based selection, gather, slice, and embedding lookup APIs across backends because backend validation gaps can occur wherever input validation is expected to be uniform but is implemented inconsistently.

llm_reasoning_guidance.important_considerations: Explore backend-specific validation gaps for index-based operations; include boundary and out-of-bound index values; compare against a CPU reference to detect missing exceptions and incorrect outputs.
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that mutate index tensors across valid and invalid ranges, execute the target operation on multiple backends, and compare exception behavior and outputs against a reference backend without hardcoding historical bug values.
